I'm happy with my current portfolio's holdings, but I have re-adjusted the weights. I'm still DCA'ing into it every week, and when my portfolio is down by any percent, I multiply that percentage by 100 and make additional deposits into it. I do have 2 "bets" in it, but they both total out to be ~1% of my portfolio combined, so even if they go to zero, oh well. My personal, non-financial advice is this: Even if you do not plan to retire early, you *need* to budget as if you were in the FIRE movement by minimize expenses to bare necessities. No subscriptions, no additional bills that are not needed, no going out, no purchasing fast food, no buying new clothes whenever you want, etc.. Even at the grocery store, you should only be spending ~$100/month/person if that.

I agree with a lot of that. No buying EVs that will lose 50% of their value, that's another for the list. 
Food is the hard one, $100/month per person is very frugal. There are two of us and we spend probably $500 / month.

@HelloJamesBond EVs? Any form of vehicle really. No car payment, no need for insurance, no need for gas (or electricity, doesn't matter). Massive savings right there. The food issue is tough, and it depends on your job. If you're not burning many calories, you can get away with spending $1.50 - $2.50/day on "food" - and yes, I put that in quotation marks on purpose. Is it healthy? Absolutely not. Can you survive? Yes. Also: neighborhood foraging, heh - there's a wealth of "free vegetables/fruits" in the urban wilds.

@FinGeek4nowTotally agree regarding car payments. I have an 18 yr old BMW and I love it, doesn’t cost me anything. I use an E bike to get to work, it’s only 3 miles each way. That’s very frugal on the food, I’m not that extreme, foraging is a great idea of you have the time.

This disconnect between fundamental progress and stock price drawdowns is exactly why pure directional equity exposure is getting dangerous right now. Market sentiment is completely decoupled from execution.
 
I got tired of watching 20-30% drawdowns wipe out months of gains, so I shifted a chunk of my liquid capital into  Basovest's  delta-neutral hedging desk earlier this year. 
Being able to capture consistent algorithmic yield while completely hedging out market directional risk has been a lifesaver during these swings. If you're still 100% exposed to directional volatility, you're taking unnecessary heat.
